fallback.text: Two groups of households, equally many, live mixed at random on a 20 × 20 grid (a torus) with one cell in ten empty. Each round, a household moves to a random empty cell when fewer than a share 'want' of its occupied neighbouring cells (the eight around it) hold its own group (Schelling 1971). At the start about half of everyone's neighbours are alike. With want = 0.25 a few moves settle everyone and the mix stays near one half; with want = 0.3, a preference that would accept being a two-to-one minority, the moves cascade and the town ends with about three quarters of every household's neighbours alike: mild individual preferences produce strong collective segregation. The picture shows the grid at the end of a run with want = 0.3.
